prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: B025 as a stand-alone prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case rests on a discovery chain that is mature and replicated: proglucagon processing and the secretion physiology of the hormone, the biology of GLP-1 and its receptor, and the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, followed by long-acting agonists with benefit shown in large randomized trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Nothing in round 1 changed my view of the science or the maturity, and no one disputed either. The chair asked whether a second achievement should share the prize. I do not support that, because each of the three names has a distinct claim to a place and sharing would force one of them out. A single part that uses all three places is the cleaner configuration.
statement.case_against: The weak point is still attribution. Priority for identifying and synthesising the active peptide is contested, Habener is outside the credited names and cannot be added, and Knudsen is left out although the acylated analogues are why the discovery reached patients. I have not been given documents that settle the priority question, and my view of the history rests on recollection. The citation should therefore say 'identification of its active form' and not claim a sole originator. I would move toward Knudsen only if the committee decides, as a matter of principle, that this citation rewards the therapeutic step. Even then I would not know which of the three should give up a place, and I do not think the discovery-side evidence supports removing any of them.

responses.point: The chair would keep Mojsov over Knudsen because the prize tradition rewards the discovery that opened the field and the active peptide is upstream of every analogue, and asks round 2 to test the GLP-1 attribution evidence first.
responses.response: This persuades me, and I have stopped treating the Knudsen question as open. The active-peptide step precedes every analogue, and a citation that reads 'identification of its active form' keeps the priority wording cautious without naming a sole originator. I disagree with one thing: describing Knudsen's work as company drug development understates it. Translational chemistry can be a prize-worthy discovery, but under a three-person limit it competes with names whose discovery-side claims are stronger. I also agree that a second achievement does not belong on this prize, since it could only enter by removing a GLP-1 name.

responses.point: Perlmann treats the missing Eshhar as more than a caveat for CAR-T, because the conceptual origin, the costimulation design and the clinical proof are separate achievements, and he regards the Walter and Mori pair as the cleaner fallback.
responses.response: I accept the Eshhar point. In round 1 I put CAR-T ahead of the unfolded protein response because the clinical evidence is not in doubt. The credited trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg does cover clinical proof and design, but the origin of the concept sits outside the names, and Rosenberg's cell-therapy work is a different line. I therefore now put B045 first among my alternatives. I still hold that B045's disease translation is incomplete. For a conceptual discovery that is a weak objection, and I withdraw it as a reason to rank it lower. I still differ with you on TOR, where the mammalian credit is as contested as GLP-1, though I agree Hall is the clear core.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps TNF blockade as her alternative, calling Feldmann and Maini a clean pair and a paradigm shift, and would keep Knudsen as the first name to revisit if the committee wants a therapeutic arm. She notes that the PERK and ATF6 branches complicate a Walter and Mori pair.
responses.response: You answered my question from round 1 only in part. Feldmann and Maini do cover the clinical proof well, but I still read the underlying cytokine biology as sitting outside the two names, so I keep B031 behind B045 and B051 for this year. Your PERK and ATF6 point is fair. Ire1, Hac1 and XBP1 are the core of the Mori and Walter discoveries, and the mammalian branches extend the pathway without weakening its premise. A citation about signalling from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus can cover that without naming more people. On Knudsen I agree she is the first name to revisit if the committee changes the principle, and I do not think the evidence yet supports that change.

responses.point: Sandberg argues that contested priority calls for careful citation wording rather than removing the only credited person tied to peptide identification, and sees CAR-T as the stronger clinical case but the unfolded protein response as the cleaner configuration.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and the wording we need is a joint description of physiology and active form. On the second point I now side with your reading that B045 is cleaner and B051 is the stronger clinical case. In round 1 I ranked B051 first among alternatives, but the incomplete credit for the concept moves it behind B045 in my judgement. If the GLP-1 priority evidence had collapsed, I would prefer B045 as the fallback single prize. I also note your co-authorship with me, which I disclose again below. It has no bearing on any credited name.

uncertainties: Whether the supplied evidence settles Mojsov's priority for the active peptide against Habener and others, and whether the citation wording is enough to manage that dispute.
Whether the committee will decide that the citation should reward the therapeutic step, which would put Knudsen in play, and which of the three would give up a place.

If GLP-1 attribution fails before the vote, whether B045 or B051 is the better fallback. My current view is B045 for its cleaner credit, with B051 limited by the missing Eshhar credit and open questions on solid tumours and toxicity.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My documented connection is co-authorship of the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and co-authors including Sandberg. None of these people is a credited name on the shortlist, and I request no recusal.
